biography.plain_text: Fabio Perini is an Italian inventor and industrialist who built an international business in machinery for converting tissue paper. Practical experience in his father’s workshop preceded his own company, founded in 1966. He later established Perini Navi and returned to paper machinery through Futura, combining mechanical invention with the creation of new businesses.

long_biography.plain_text:
Fabio Perini learned to imagine a machine before drawing it, a habit inherited from watching his father work. The inventor eventually employed a draughtsman to put those mental pictures on paper. His first patented device regulated movement in a paper machine; the initial version failed, but the next worked.

Selling his original machinery company gave him the means to pursue a different project in Brazil. In Joinville, he learned about precast concrete construction and developed industrial premises. Perini Business Park initially aimed to provide rented space for small enterprises. Larger tenants changed its direction, turning a modest workshop concept into a substantial industrial community.
